name: MailboxMCP
title: Mailbox
description: Give an Agent one inbox as tools: list its threads, read one, reply in it, send a new message, keep a draft
whenToUse: Let an Agent work a mailbox: see the conversations waiting in one inbox, read a thread in full, answer it so the reply lands in the same conversation, start a new message, or keep a draft for a person to send. Pick it for an Agent that manages email on the inbox's behalf. It works one inbox, the one its Mailbox credential names, and never another. Attach by a service edge to the Agent; it is not a data-flow step.

outputs.name: overview
outputs.description: The inbox at a glance: reachable, unanswered, drafts, volume

outputs.name: unanswered
outputs.description: Threads whose last message is theirs, oldest first

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: mail
package.packageFile:
# MAIL — the platform's own mailbox (docs/unoverse/mail/README.md): an address in, a
# conversation out. Inboxes on the platform's domain, each a list of threads, each thread its
# messages in order; a reply goes back into the thread it answers.
#
# TWO NODES. MailboxMessages reads an inbox as a step; MailboxMCP gives an attached Agent the
# mailbox as tools: list the threads, read one, reply, send, draft. Both reach the mailbox
# service THROUGH THE ENGINE at loopback (`scope.engineUrl` + /mail/...), the way the document
# nodes reach /documents: a node's call must be https or loopback, and the engine holds the
# service. THE INBOX IS THE CREDENTIAL (credentials/mailboxCredential.yaml, owner ruling
# 2026-09-20): address, name and the AWS account that receives and sends for it, set once on
# the credentials screen. Both nodes name it; neither has an inbox field.
#
# NOT the `email` package. SendGridEmail is one-way mail with no thread; this is two-way and
# threaded, and a saved workflow storing either type keeps meaning what it meant.

name: mail
displayName: Mailbox
description: >-
  Read and answer email from an inbox of the platform's own: threads, messages, replies and
  drafts, for a step or for an Agent
version: 0.1.0
category: communication
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

features:
  - Read an inbox's threads, newest first, with each thread's last message
  - "Give an Agent the mailbox as tools: list, read, reply, send, draft"
  - A reply carries In-Reply-To and References, so it lands in the same conversation everywhere

allowedHosts:
  # LOOPBACK ONLY, numeric form: every call goes to the engine's own listener, which serves the
  # mailbox. No third-party host, ever.
  - 127.0.0.1

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  transport: [json]

credentials.googleClientCredential.yaml:
# THE PLATFORM'S ONE GOOGLE APPLICATION, saved once and never again.
#
# NOBODY CHOOSES THIS, which is why `visibility: internal` keeps it out of the credentials
# picker. It is collected in the panel that opens under the Connect button, the first time
# anyone on this platform connects a Gmail mailbox, and never seen again.
#
# It is a credential rather than a setting so it is encrypted at rest with everything else, and
# so it can be saved from the screen a person is already standing on instead of by editing a
# file and restarting.

name: googleClientCredential
displayName: Google application
category: Platform setup
visibility: internal
description: The OAuth client that makes Google's approval screen say unoverse. Collected once, under the Connect button.
documentationUrl: https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials

properties:
  - name: clientId
    displayName: Client ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: From the OAuth client you created in Google Cloud.
    placeholder: 1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com

  - name: clientSecret
    displayName: Client secret
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: From the same page.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.mailboxCredential.yaml:
# PICK THE SERVICE, LOG IN, DONE (owner ruling 2026-09-20: "stop overcomplicating"; "I should
# see Outlook, I should see Gmail"). The same shape as adding an account on a phone: name it,
# choose Gmail or Outlook, approve on their own screen. Everything else comes back from them
# and is never typed.
#
# The Agent then acts on that mailbox with nobody signed in, which is what the grant is for —
# the same way a phone keeps fetching mail long after you logged into it once.

name: mailboxCredential
displayName: Mailbox
category: Communication
description: A mailbox an Agent reads and answers. Connect Gmail or Outlook.

properties:
  - name: connect
    displayName: Mailbox
    type: connect
    required: true
    secret: false
    description: Choose where the mailbox lives and approve access on their screen.
    connect: /mail/connect
    connected: address
    providers:
      - { id: google, label: Gmail }
      - { id: microsoft, label: Outlook }

  # ── Filled by the service when you connect. Never typed, never shown again. ─────────────
  - name: address
    displayName: Address
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The mailbox you connected.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

  - name: provider
    displayName: Service
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Which service holds it.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

  - name: refreshToken
    displayName: Grant
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: The lasting permission this mailbox gave.
    "ui:dependencies": { __never: true }

shared.schema.yaml:
# TOOL DISCOVERY, as DATA: what an attached Agent reads before touching the mailbox. The
# wording IS the routing: a model reads these descriptions when choosing a tool, so rephrasing
# is a behaviour change, never a tidy-up. The argument shapes are what the model fills in.
#
# Written as plain YAML rather than a `return { ... }` expression: a constant is data.

mailbox:
  name: Mailbox
  version: "0.1.0"
  description: One email inbox, as threads and messages. Read what is waiting, answer in the thread, start a message, keep a draft.
  instructions: |-
    MAILBOX PROTOCOL:
    - list_threads first, to see what is waiting. It is cheap and carries no bodies.
    - read_thread before answering anything: a reply is judged against the whole conversation,
      not its last line.
    - reply answers IN the thread, to the person who wrote, with the others copied. Use it for
      every answer to a message you have read. Never start a new message to answer an old one.
    - send starts a NEW conversation with someone; only for a message that answers nothing.
    - save_draft when a person should look before it goes. A draft is not sent.
    - A sent message comes back with state "sent" and its id. State "failed" carries the reason;
      say so rather than claiming it went.
    - You work ONE inbox. You cannot read or send from any other.
  methods:
    list_threads:
      description: >-
        The conversations in the inbox, newest first, each with its subject, who is in it, how
        many messages, when the last one arrived, and that last message's sender and direction.
        No bodies: read_thread gives those. An empty list means nothing is waiting, which is
        normal.
      input:
        type: object
        required: []
        properties:
          since:
            type: string
            description: Only threads with a message after this time, as an ISO date. Leave out for the newest regardless.
          limit:
            type: number
            description: How many threads, newest first. Default 20, at most 200.
    read_thread:
      description: >-
        One conversation in full: every message in order, each with sender, recipients,
        subject, the text, and its attachments as links that open for a while. Call it before
        replying.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [threadId]
        properties:
          threadId:
            type: string
            description: The thread's id, from list_threads.
    reply:
      description: >-
        Answer a message in its own thread. The reply goes to the message's sender, with the
        other people on it copied, under the thread's subject, and carries the headers that make
        it land in the same conversation in their mail client. Comes back with state "sent" and
        the message's id, or "failed" with the reason.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [messageId, text]
        properties:
          messageId:
            type: string
            description: The id of the message being answered, from read_thread. Usually the last one from the other side.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The reply, as plain text. Write the whole message; it is sent as written.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same reply as HTML, when the message needs formatting. The text is still sent alongside.
    send:
      description: >-
        Start a NEW conversation: a message from the inbox to one or more people. Not for
        answering a message, which is reply. Comes back with state "sent" and the message's id,
        or "failed" with the reason.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [to, subject, text]
        properties:
          to:
            type: string
            description: Who it goes to, one or more addresses separated by commas. A name may be given as "Name <address>".
          cc:
            type: string
            description: Optional. Who is copied, the same way.
          subject:
            type: string
            description: The subject line.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The message, as plain text.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same message as HTML.
    save_draft:
      description: >-
        Keep a message without sending it, for a person to read and send. Comes back with state
        "draft" and the draft's id. Nothing leaves the inbox.
      input:
        type: object
        required: [to, subject, text]
        properties:
          to:
            type: string
            description: Who it is for, one or more addresses separated by commas.
          cc:
            type: string
            description: Optional. Who would be copied.
          subject:
            type: string
            description: The subject line.
          text:
            type: string
            description: The message, as plain text.
          html:
            type: string
            description: Optional. The same message as HTML.

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order. `response` is the overview door's
# reply: { account, health, threads, unanswered, drafts, volume }.
#
# THE SHAPING LIVES IN shared/overview.yaml, because the OTHER mail node emits the same picture
# of the same inbox and two copies of a projection drift. `unanswered` stays the rows as the
# mailbox states them, for a step that acts on one rather than draws it.

- emit: overview
  value: { $ref: overview#screen }

# The rows as the mailbox states them, for a step that acts on a thread rather than draws it.
- emit: unanswered
  value: "return (response && response.unanswered) || []"
files.api/run.yaml:
# THE GRAPH'S CHANNEL: what this node does when the workflow runs it. One read of the inbox
# the credential names, through the engine at loopback (package.yaml says why).
#
# THE MAILBOX IS THE SOURCE: the door asks Google or Microsoft at the moment it is asked, and
# nothing is stored on our side. Which provider answers is the credential's business, so
# nothing here knows or cares.

- name: overview
  method: GET
  url: >-
    return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/inboxes/'
      + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase())
      + '/overview'
  transport: json

  timeoutMs: 30000

  # The door answers 404 with `{ error }` for an address no credential names, which is the
  # common mistake (a box whose credential was never attached). Without this the node would
  # emit an empty overview and look like a working mailbox with nothing in it.
  error:
    when: "return !!response.error"
    message: "return response.error"
files.api/service.yaml:
# THE FIVE TOOLS an attached Agent gets, each one call to the mailbox through the engine at
# loopback (package.yaml says why). The inbox is the CREDENTIAL'S address, never a tool argument:
# the author decides which inbox an Agent works by attaching a Mailbox credential, the model only
# decides what to do in it. A model that could name another inbox would route around the author.
#
# Every door answers { error } on a miss, so every call declares the same error block; without
# it a thread that does not exist would look like an empty one.

getSchema:
  description: Tool discovery for the mailbox
  calls: []
  returns: { $ref: schema#mailbox }

list_threads:
  description: >-
    The conversations in the inbox, newest first, each with its last message's sender, subject
    and time. No bodies. An empty list means nothing is waiting.
  calls:
    - name: threads
      method: GET
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/inboxes/' + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase()) + '/threads'"
      transport: json
      query:
        since: "{{ params.since }}"
        limit: "return String(Math.min(Number(params.limit || 20), 200))"
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error"
  returns: >-
    return { ok: true, threads: (response.threads || []).map(t => ({
      id: t.id, subject: t.subject, participants: t.participants, messageCount: t.messageCount,
      lastMessageAt: t.lastMessageAt, last: t.last
    })) }

read_thread:
  description: >-
    One conversation in full: every message in order with sender, recipients, subject, text and
    attachments as links. Call before replying.
  calls:
    - name: thread
      method: GET
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/threads/' + encodeURIComponent(String(params.threadId || ''))"
      transport: json
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error"
  # The Agent reads the TEXT of a message, never its html: html is for a screen, and it is the
  # part that fills a context with markup nobody reads.
  returns: >-
    return { ok: true, id: response.id, subject: response.subject, participants: response.participants,
      messages: (response.messages || []).map(m => ({
        id: m.id, direction: m.direction, state: m.state, from: m.from, to: m.to, cc: m.cc,
        subject: m.subject, text: m.text, attachments: m.attachments,
        at: m.receivedAt || m.sentAt || m.createdAt
      })) }

reply:
  description: >-
    Answer a message in its own thread, to its sender with the others copied. State "sent" with
    the message's id, or "failed" with the reason.
  calls:
    - name: reply
      method: POST
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/messages/' + encodeURIComponent(String(params.messageId || '')) + '/reply'"
      transport: json
      body:
        text: "{{ params.text }}"
        html: "return params.html || undefined"
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error"
  returns: "return { ok: response.state === 'sent', id: response.id, threadId: response.threadId, state: response.state, error: response.error || null }"

send:
  description: >-
    Start a new conversation from the inbox. State "sent" with the message's id, or "failed"
    with the reason.
  calls:
    - name: send
      method: POST
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/inboxes/' + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase()) + '/messages'"
      transport: json
      body:
        to: "{{ params.to }}"
        cc: "return params.cc || undefined"
        subject: "{{ params.subject }}"
        text: "{{ params.text }}"
        html: "return params.html || undefined"
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error"
  returns: "return { ok: response.state === 'sent', id: response.id, threadId: response.threadId, state: response.state, error: response.error || null }"

save_draft:
  description: >-
    Keep a message for a person to send. State "draft" with the draft's id; nothing leaves.
  calls:
    - name: draft
      method: POST
      url: "return scope.engineUrl + '/mail/inboxes/' + encodeURIComponent(String(credentials.mailboxCredential.address || '').trim().toLowerCase()) + '/drafts'"
      transport: json
      body:
        to: "{{ params.to }}"
        cc: "return params.cc || undefined"
        subject: "{{ params.subject }}"
        text: "{{ params.text }}"
        html: "return params.html || undefined"
      error:
        when: "return !!response.error"
        message: "return response.error"
  returns: "return { ok: true, id: response.id, threadId: response.threadId, state: response.state }"
files.config.yaml:
# No options: the whole node is a function of the Mailbox credential attached to it.
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties: {}
"ui:order": []
files.interface.yaml:
# A SERVICE NODE THAT ALSO RUNS, the shape HubspotMCP has: the graph may run it and read the
# inbox's state from its output, AND an Agent may attach to it and call its tools. The two
# channels never cross: `api/run.yaml` + `api/events.yaml` are the graph's, `api/service.yaml`
# is the Agent's.

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    required: true
    description: Trigger to fire the node

outputs:
  - name: overview
    type: object
    description: "The inbox at a glance: reachable, unanswered, drafts, volume"
  - name: unanswered
    type: array
    description: Threads whose last message is theirs, oldest first

# THE INBOX IS THE CREDENTIAL: which mailbox this node reads and this Agent works is decided by
# the credential the author attaches, never by a config field and never by the model.
credentials:
  - name: mailboxCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Mailbox

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mailbox
    serviceType: mcp
    # PROVIDES. The node offers these tools to a consuming Agent.
    isService: true
    description: >-
      One inbox as tools for an Agent: list_threads, read_thread, reply, send, save_draft.
    instructions: >-
      List the threads before answering anything, and read a thread in full before replying to
      it: a reply is judged against the whole conversation, not its last line. Always reply IN
      the thread with `reply`; `send` starts a NEW conversation and is never the way to answer
      one. Save a draft instead of sending when a person should look first. A send comes back
      with state "sent" or "failed" with the reason: never say a message went when it failed.
      You work one inbox and cannot reach another.
    # `getSchema` is tool DISCOVERY, a meta-method the harness calls, and must not be listed.
    methods:
      - list_threads
      - read_thread
      - reply
      - send
      - save_draft
files.node.yaml:
type: MailboxMCP
# Every call settles and there is no CONTINUE port: a PromiseNode.
kind: PromiseNode

name: Mailbox
category: Communication
color: "#0F766E"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1751366180/gravity/icons/gravityIcon.png

# Drawn as a service node: it is ATTACHED to an Agent over a service edge, never wired in
# sequence, so the compact card is the honest shape.
template: service

description: >-
  Give an Agent one inbox as tools: list its threads, read one, reply in it, send a new
  message, keep a draft

whenToUse: >-
  Let an Agent work a mailbox: see the conversations waiting in one inbox, read a thread in
  full, answer it so the reply lands in the same conversation, start a new message, or keep a
  draft for a person to send. Pick it for an Agent that manages email on the inbox's behalf. It
  works one inbox, the one its Mailbox credential names, and never another. Attach by a service edge to
  the Agent; it is not a data-flow step.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # NOT cacheable: the mailbox changes, and reply and send are side effects a reuse would skip.
  #
  # `emitsExternally` is deliberately NOT declared: the engine withholds an emitting NODE on a
  # test run, but a tool an Agent calls over a service edge is not a node run, so declaring it
  # here would claim a control that does not act. A test run of an Agent with this node attached
  # can send a real reply. That gap is named in docs/unoverse/mail/README.md.
  cacheable: false

# THE PANEL'S TAB (owner ruling 2026-09-20): a person's face on this node, a tab beside
# Configuration and Debug. `mailbox` is the shared marketplace component
# (design/marketplace/components/mailbox); the tab RUNS this node and draws what its
# `overview` output emits, so the screen and a workflow step read the same thing through the
# same run and the same events table. Settings stay on the Configuration tab.
menu:
  - label: Mailbox
    component: mailbox
    output: overview
files.test.yaml:
# THE RUN, which is the channel this node is now reached through by both a workflow step and
# its own panel tab. It reads the inbox its Mailbox credential names (the bench takes the
# credential's fields from the workspace .env) and emits the inbox's state.
#
# The service channel is deliberately NOT the fixture: `reply` and `send` put a real message
# in a real person's inbox, and a bench that does that is not one anyone runs twice.
#
# Shape assertions only. An inbox holding nothing is a working mailbox with nothing in it,
# which is a legitimate answer rather than a failure.
testData:
  config: {}

  inputs:
    signal: {}

  expect:
    overview: >-
      return !!output.overview
        && typeof output.overview.address === 'string'
        && ['Working', 'Failing'].indexOf(output.overview.stateLabel) >= 0
        && Array.isArray(output.overview.unanswered)
        && Array.isArray(output.overview.volume)
        && output.overview.volume.length === 7
    unanswered: "return Array.isArray(output.unanswered)"
